les: Leonardo da Vinci teken wat hy sien
kaps_punt: Gevallestudies: Die bydraes van: Leonardo da Vinci

items.bewering: Leonardo da Vinci was 'n kunstenaar van Italië in die tyd van die Renaissance.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Leonardo da Vinci' (born 15 April 1452 in or near Vinci, Tuscany; died 2 May 1519 at Clos Lucé, Amboise, France); Museo Leonardiano, Vinci (museoleonardiano.it biography); Britannica, 'Vitruvian Man', calls him an epitome of the Renaissance. Italy was not yet one state, but 'van Italië' as a place of origin is the normal description.

items.bewering: Daardie tyd was die 15de en die 16de eeu.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Renaissance', lead: 'variously defined as covering the 15th and 16th centuries' or, more broadly, 'from the 14th century to the 17th'. The lesson gives the narrower, recognised definition. Note for the human: Britannica Dictionary (learnersdictionary.com) and Dictionary.com give the broader 14th-17th span, and Oxford Learner's gives the 14th-16th, so this is one convention among several rather than the only answer. Not wrong; flagged only so nobody is surprised if a learner meets a different span elsewhere.

items.bewering: Leonardo het geleef en gewerk in dieselfde jare as die reise van Dias en Da Gama om die suidpunt van Afrika.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Bartolomeu Dias' (sailed 1487, rounded the southern tip 1488); Museo Galileo, 'The circumnavigation of Africa' (mostre.museogalileo.it); St John's College Cambridge, 'Bartolomeu Dias and Vasco da Gama' (Da Gama left Lisbon 8 July 1497, rounded the Cape 22 November 1497, reached Calicut May 1498). Leonardo lived 1452-1519 and was working in Milan in both periods (Last Supper c. 1495-1498).

items.bewering: Hy het geskilder en ook na byna alles rondom hom gekyk. Hy wou weet hoe elke ding werk en hoekom dit so lyk.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Science and inventions of Leonardo da Vinci' (close observation of nature as the central theme of his life); British Library description of the Codex Arundel (subjects include mechanics, flow of rivers, astronomy, optics, architecture, flight of birds). 'Byna alles' is a fair summary of that range.

items.bewering: Leonardo het lank na 'n ding gekyk voor hy dit geteken het.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Science and inventions of Leonardo da Vinci'; Royal Collection Trust, 'Leonardo's study of anatomy' (rct.uk) - his drawings rest on sustained observation, e.g. the arm drawn in successive positions on RCIN 919004.

items.bewering: Hy het baie meer as ander op sy eie oë vertrou en minder op ou boeke.
items.bron: Leonardo's own notebooks: he signed himself 'disscepolo della sperientia' (disciple of experience) and called himself 'omo sanza lettere' (unlettered man), and called those who only quote others 'trumpeters and reciters of the works of others' - quoted in Charles Nicholl, London Review of Books vol. 26 no. 24 (2004), and Walter Isaacson, 'Leonardo da Vinci' (excerpt on bookbrowse.com); Leonardo/ISAST (leonardo.info). Nuance, not a fault: scholarship (Utrecht University, 'Leonardo: Disciple of experience - and of books') shows he did read and use books; the lesson's comparative 'meer ... en minder' rather than 'nie' is the careful form and should be kept.

items.bewering: Sy notaboeke is vol sketse, en langs baie van die tekeninge staan notas.
items.bron: British Library, Codex Arundel (Arundel MS 263), digitised 570 pages: 'papers ... covering science, art and personal notes, with diagrams and brief texts', written in mirror writing; Royal Collection Trust anatomical sheets (e.g. RCIN 919000, 919004) carry text beside the drawings.

items.bewering: Die teken was self sy manier om 'n ding te verstaan.
items.bron: Royal Collection Trust, 'Leonardo's study of anatomy' (rct.uk): he analysed the body through drawing, building up the hand layer by layer and stripping the shoulder down in stages, 'adopting a range of illustrative techniques to make his drawings as clear as possible'; Science Museum's Jim Bennett (VOA report): 'It is the drawing, the understanding and the imagination that is important.'

items.bewering: Jy kan nie 'n voël se vlerk teken as jy nie noukeurig daarna gekyk het nie.
items.bron: Illustrative statement, read as 'draw accurately'; it fits his practice: Smithsonian Torch, '400 years before the airplane, Leonardo da Vinci took to the sky' (torch.si.edu, 2013) - the Codex on the Flight of Birds (c. 1505) records his observations of birds in flight. Not a factual claim that could mislead; mapping holds.

items.bewering: Leonardo het dit [die Mona Lisa] geskilder en ook Die Laaste Avondmaal.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'The Last Supper (Leonardo)' (Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan, c. 1495-1498, commissioned by Ludovico Sforza); Britannica 'Last Supper: At a Glance' (britannica.com/print/article/2235816); discoveringdavinci.com, 'Mona Lisa (Louvre)'; 2010 Louvre/C2RMF study of seven Leonardo paintings including the Mona Lisa (reported by NBC News, Physics World).

items.bewering: Hy het lig en skaduwee so gebruik dat die mense in sy skilderye rond lyk.
items.bron: National Gallery London, glossary 'Chiaroscuro' (nationalgallery.org.uk): Leonardo used tonal contrast 'to give a vivid impression of the three-dimensionality of his figures'; Louvre 2019 Leonardo exhibition booklet, section 'Light, Shade, Relief'.

items.bewering: Die dinge agter hulle is kleiner en vaer, en daarom lyk die plat prent na 'n werklike plek.
items.bron: discoveringdavinci.com, perspective notes and Mona Lisa background analysis (winding road = linear perspective, fading detail and blue-green haze on distant mountains = aerial perspective); Leonardo's own notes on distant objects appearing bluer and fainter (gallerix.ru, 'Perspective techniques in the works of Leonardo da Vinci'). Mapping checked: a learner reasoning on from this ('far things look smaller and hazier, so a painter shows them that way') reaches the correct idea of linear plus aerial perspective. The comparison holds.

items.bewering: Hy het dooie liggame ondersoek en geteken wat hy daar gesien het.
items.bron: Royal Collection Trust, 'Leonardo's study of anatomy' (rct.uk): working with Marcantonio della Torre at Pavia in winter 1510-11 he 'may have dissected as many as 20 corpses that winter'; Artlyst: more than 30 human corpses between 1507 and 1513.

items.bewering: Sy tekeninge wys spiere, beentjies en gewrigte, soos die elmboog waar die arm buig.
items.bron: Royal Collection Trust RCIN 919004 'The bones of the arm and leg' (eight skeletal drawings of the arm at different degrees of flexion at the elbow, showing the olecranon moving into the olecranon fossa) and RCIN 919000 'The bones of the foot; the bones and muscles of the arm' (biceps bending the elbow and turning the forearm). Cleveland Clinic, 'Elbow joint': the elbow hinges to bend and straighten the arm.

items.bewering: Hulle is so noukeurig dat kenners hulle vandag nog bewonder.
items.bron: Royal Collection Trust RCIN 919000: his observation of the double action of biceps 'would be two centuries before Leonardo's observation was repeated'; PBS NOVA, 'Anatomy professor uses 500-year-old da Vinci drawings to guide cadaver dissection' (Boston University).

items.bewering: Leonardo het ook planne geteken vir masjiene wat sou vlieg en vir masjiene vir oorlog.
items.bron: Smithsonian Torch (torch.si.edu, 2013): Codex on the Flight of Birds and an ornithopter model based on Manuscript B folio 74 (Institut de France); History Hit, '10 of Leonardo da Vinci's most important inventions' (ornithopter, helical air screw, giant crossbow, armoured vehicle in the Codex Arundel).

items.bewering: Hy het dit [die vliegtuig] nie uitgevind nie en 'n tekening is nog nie 'n masjien wat werk nie.
items.bron: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum via torch.si.edu (2013): his flight sketches 'predate the invention of the airplane by 400 years' and were shown beside the Wright brothers' 1903 Flyer; History Hit: the materials would have been too heavy and human muscle power insufficient for his flying machines to fly.

items.bewering: Die meeste van sy masjiene is in sy leeftyd nooit gebou nie.
items.bron: Franklin Institute curator Troy Collins (CBS Philadelphia): 'Most of Leonardo's inventions were actually never built'; Museum of Science and Industry Manchester director Tony Hill (road.cc): 'Most of his works were never made'; History Hit: the giant and rapid-fire crossbows were built only in 2003 and 2013-15. 'Die meeste' rather than 'geen' is the correct careful form - some of his work was realised in his lifetime - and should be kept.

items.bewering: Leonardo se werk wys wat die keerpunt van die Renaissance beteken het.
items.blok: Wat Leonardo oor die keerpunt wys
items.bron: Interpretive framing, checked as such. Britannica ('Vitruvian Man' and Leonardo entry, britannica.com/print/article/336408): his skill and intelligence 'perhaps more than that of any other figure, epitomized the Renaissance humanist ideal'; Smarthistory (Zucker and Harris, via brewminate.com) and artyfactory.com on Renaissance naturalism: artists used perspective, anatomy and observation of nature to make art 'more like real life'. Nuance for the human, not a fault: Renaissance humanism also meant reviving ancient Greek and Roman texts, so 'observation over old books' (block 'Hy teken wat hy sien') describes Leonardo more than it describes every Renaissance thinker - which the lesson itself signals with 'baie meer as ander'. Keep that comparative; a version saying the Renaissance as a whole turned away from old books would be false.

items.bewering: Hy het self gaan kyk en self gemeet en dan geteken wat hy sien. Daarna het hy gevra hoekom die ding so werk.
items.blok: Wat Leonardo oor die keerpunt wys
items.bron: Britannica, 'Vitruvian Man': he 'spent months measuring a number of young men', and the measurements, though attributed to Vitruvius, are mostly his own findings; Royal Collection Trust RCIN 919000/919004: from drawing the arm he worked out how biceps bends the elbow and turns the forearm - observation followed by explanation of mechanism.

items.bewering: notaboek: 'n Boek waarin iemand sy eie sketse en notas bymekaar hou.
items.bron: Learner's Dictionary (Britannica), 'notebook': a book with blank pages used for writing notes; Dictionary.com, 'notebook'. Including sketches suits Leonardo's notebooks (British Library, Codex Arundel). Accurate as a simple definition.

items.bewering: skets: 'n Vinnige tekening wat 'n ding se vorm en dele wys.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster, 'sketch': 'a rough drawing representing the chief features of an object or scene and often made as a preliminary study'. 'Vinnige' and 'vorm en dele' map onto 'rough' and 'chief features'.

items.bewering: gewrig: Die plek in die liggaam waar twee of meer stukke been bymekaar kom.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster (kids' and medical entries, 'joint'): the point of contact of two bones / elements of the skeleton; NCBI StatPearls on hinge joints ('two or more bones'); Cleveland Clinic, 'Elbow joint': the elbow connects the humerus to the radius and ulna - three bones, consistent with 'twee of meer'.

opsomming: All 23 checkable claims hold against museum, library and reference sources, with nothing contradicted or uncertain; the lesson has no real analogy (its one comparison, flat painting to real place, maps correctly) and one superlative ('die meeste van sy masjiene'), which is correctly hedged. Two things should stay as they are: 'baie meer as ander ... minder op ou boeke' must remain comparative, because Renaissance humanism also revived ancient texts, and 'die 15de en die 16de eeu' is one recognised definition of the Renaissance while others give 14th-17th.
